mediaWork.title: Deadline
mediaWork.focusOrTheme: Illinois Governor George Ryan's struggle with the state's flawed death penalty system, prompted by exonerations and Northwestern University investigations, culminating in his commutation of all death sentences.
mediaWork.summaryNotes: The story of Illinois Governor George Ryan, who, in the days before leaving office, commuted the sentences of all 167 inmates on the state's death row after a commission found that the system was too flawed to ensure against error.

mediaItems.focusOrTheme: Illinois Governor George Ryan's struggle with the state's flawed death penalty system, prompted by exonerations and Northwestern University investigations, culminating in his commutation of all death sentences.
mediaItems.summaryNotes: Documents Illinois Governor George Ryan's decision to commute all death sentences in Illinois after a series of wrongful convictions were uncovered. Features interviews with Governor Ryan, his staff, journalists, and lawyers.
mediaItems.keyQuotes:
Interviews with Governor Ryan, his staff, journalists, lawyers, potentially exonerees or their families.

Footage of the clemency hearings and Ryan's final announcement commuting the sentences.

featuredIndividuals.narrativeSummary: The documentary features several Illinois death row exonerees who were exonerated or had their sentences commuted by Gov. Ryan. Their cases highlight flaws in the criminal justice system.
